bullets.text: Customer retention became a key strategic initiative. Management considers policies in force useful to measure growth and believes reducing expirations is its biggest opportunity. Cancellations remained relatively constant, and new applications fell about 8%.
Q3 net income rose 34% to $409.6M; YTD net income reached $1.25B (+12%); Q3 CR was 87.3 versus 90.4 in 2005; YTD CR improved to 86.4 from 87.2.
Companywide net written premium grew less than 1% in Q3, decelerating from nearly 2% year to date. Growth lagged expectations in the so-called "soft" market. Profitability remained strong.
Strong margins permit lowering rates where appropriate to lengthen policy life, aiming for a 96 or better CR; earned premium per auto policy fell ~3% from rate decreases and mix shifts.

The industry continued adjusting to low accident frequency and bodily injury severity. Progressive experienced about 3% lower earned premiums per auto policy, resulting from rate decreases and business mix shifts.

Growth lagged expectations in the so-called "soft" market. Amid downward price pressure, departing customers found lower prices at policy expiration. The business faced little near-term pressure for premium inflation.

Homesite agreements enable independent agents and direct channels to offer homeowners, renters, and condominium policies. A Liberty Mutual agreement provides Direct Internet homeowners coverage, supporting Progressive's customer retention strategy.

Three-state homeowners pilots with Homesite will begin in agent and direct channels. A Liberty Mutual multi-state pilot begins shortly for Direct Internet, and Direct may seek other home insurance underwriters as necessary.

Progressive established Net Promoter Score to evaluate customer satisfaction at a granular level, emphasized treating customers as we would like to be treated, and embraced challenges to become Consumers’ #1 Choice for Auto Insurance.
